title: The origin fiber is the stationary-phase contribution
statement:
Use the finite-field and coefficient datum of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], with $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{k_0}$ and $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$, and the $\Qlb$-Weil sheaves of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], lisse in the sense of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves]. The notation $j_{!*}\mathcal M[1]=(j_*\mathcal M)[1]$ uses the ordinary sheaf middle extension of [def-wf-middle-extension], not the derived direct image. Cohomology is geometric compactly supported cohomology over $k$, with its Weil action, in the convention of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology]. Local inertia and its action are those of [d-real-boundary].

Let $\psi$ be an additive character of $k_0$, let
$j:U_0\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$ and
$j':U'_0\hookrightarrow A'_0$ be dense open immersions into
the line and the dual line, and let $\mathcal M$ and $\mathcal M'$ be
lisse Weil sheaves on $U_0$ and $U'_0$ whose middle extensions
correspond as Weil complexes under the Fourier transform of [def-fd-transform]:
$\operatorname{FT}_\psi(j_{!*}\mathcal M[1])\cong j'_{!*}\mathcal M'[1]$,
i.e. $\operatorname{FT}_\psi((j_*\mathcal M)[1])\cong(j'_*\mathcal M')[1]$.
Then the degree $-1$ part of the fiber at
the origin of the dual line is the $H_c^1$-term of the local Fourier
exact sequence at the origin:

$$
\mathcal H^{-1}\Bigl(\operatorname{FT}_\psi(j_{!*}\mathcal M[1])_{0'}\Bigr)
\cong H_c^1(\mathbf A^1_{k_0},j_*\mathcal M)\;\cong\;(j'_*\mathcal M')_{0'}\;=\;\bigl(\mathcal M'_{\bar\eta}\bigr)^{I_{0'}},
$$

the last identification being the invariants of the local inertia
$I_{0'}$ at the origin of the dual line (acting trivially if $0'\in U'_0$): the
stationary phase term is therefore the origin part of the transformed
middle extension. Moreover $H_c^2(\mathbf A^1_{k_0},j_*\mathcal M)=0$.
All these identifications are *Frobenius-equivariant*: the origin $0'$
is a $k_0$-rational point, and the geometric Frobenius of $k_0$ acting
on $H_c^1(\mathbf A^1_{k_0},j_*\mathcal M)$ corresponds to the local
Frobenius $F_{0'}$ on the stalk $(j'_*\mathcal M')_{0'}$ of the Weil
sheaf $j'_*\mathcal M'$, and to the action of a Frobenius lift on
$(\mathcal M'_{\bar\eta})^{I_{0'}}$.

proof.text: Put $F=j_*\mathcal M$ and $G=j'_*\mathcal M'$, ordinary sheaves as in [def-wf-middle-extension], and write $T=\operatorname{FT}_\psi(F[1])$. The Fourier-partner hypothesis is an isomorphism $\alpha:T\xrightarrow{\sim}G[1]$ of Weil complexes; no nonexceptionality or irreducibility argument is needed to obtain it. Apply [lem-fd-stalk-at-origin] to $F[1]$. It gives $T_{\bar0'}\cong R\Gamma_c(\mathbf A^1_k,F)[2]$, whose degree $-1$ and $0$ cohomology are $H_c^1(\mathbf A^1_k,F)$ and $H_c^2(\mathbf A^1_k,F)$, in the convention of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology]. Since that statement names the isomorphism only as canonical, Steps 3–4 use the explicit isomorphism $a:T_{\bar0'}\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_c(\mathbf A^1_k,F)[2]$ constructed in Step 3 from cited statements alone; $\mathcal H^{-1}(a)$ and $\mathcal H^0(a)$ then identify the source's degree $-1$ and $0$ cohomology with $H_c^1$ and $H_c^2$. The two shifts are the middle-extension shift $[1]$ and the rank-one Fourier normalization $[1]$.

source.place: paragraph 2: origin stalk and the two cohomological degrees; paragraph 1 replaced by the current statement's Fourier-partner hypothesis

proof.text: The kernel trivialization used at the origin is compatible with Weil structures. Indeed, by [def-fd-kernel] its restriction there is the Artin–Schreier sheaf for $x\cdot0=0$. In the covering of [def-fd-artin-schreier-sheaf] this is $T^p-T=0$, the disjoint union of the constant sections $T=a$, $a\in\mathbf F_p$. Its pushforward is the constant space of functions on $\mathbf F_p$; its specified character-isotypic summand is a constant line, trivialized by its character function normalized to have value $1$ at $0$. All those sections and that function are defined over $k_0$, so geometric Frobenius fixes this trivialization. Tensoring with this line is therefore the unit identification as a Weil sheaf, rather than merely as a geometric sheaf.

source.place: paragraph 2: trivialization of the zero-function kernel over the rational origin

proof.text: The exchange isomorphism defining $a$ commutes with Frobenius. Apply [lem-fix-weil-operations] at coefficients $E$ (a common finite field of definition for the sheaves and character) and then $\Qlb$: pullback, tensor, compact-support direct image and their exchange maps have their canonical Weil structures and equivariant comparison maps. Here $p_2:\mathbf A^1\times\mathbf A'^1\to\mathbf A'^1$ and the origin inclusion descend to $k_0$ and are separated of finite type; the bounded constructible domains are exactly those of the Fourier transform in [def-fd-transform] and the origin formula in Step 1. Define $a$ explicitly. Let $e=\bar0':\operatorname{Spec}k\to\mathbf A'^1_k$ be the geometric point over the rational origin, $p_2':\mathbf A^1_k\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ the base change of $p_2$ and $e'=(\mathrm{id},0'):\mathbf A^1_k\to\mathbf A^1_k\times\mathbf A'^1_k$. Put $a$ equal to the composite $T_{\bar0'}=Le^*Rp_{2!}(p_1^*F[1]\otimes^L\mathcal K_\psi)[1]\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Ex}_!}Rp'_{2!}Le'^*(p_1^*F[1]\otimes^L\mathcal K_\psi)[1]\cong Rp'_{2!}(F[1]\otimes^L e'^*\mathcal K_\psi)[1]\cong R\Gamma_c(\mathbf A^1_k,F)[2]$. The middle map is the pullback–tensor and composition comparison ($p_1e'=\mathrm{id}$). The last map uses $e'^*\mathcal K_\psi=\mathcal L_{\psi,b\circ e'}=\mathcal L_{\psi,0}$ (the pullback compatibility stated in [def-fd-kernel]) with the trivialization of Step 2, and then the shift. The exchange $\operatorname{Ex}_!$ is an isomorphism by [thm-cbc-qbar]: $p_2$ is separated of finite type, $e$ is arbitrary, and the four schemes are noetherian, finite-dimensional and have $\ell$ invertible. So $a$ is an isomorphism realizing [lem-fd-stalk-at-origin], taken from no proof. Thus $a\theta_T=\theta_{R\Gamma_c(F)[2]}\,g^*(a)$ in the Weil-pair notation of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Since $\kappa(0')=k_0$, this gives the same geometric Frobenius of $k_0$ on cohomology as the local stalk Frobenius at $0'$, with no residue-degree power.

source.place: paragraph 2: Frobenius-equivariance of base change, tensor unit, and origin identification

proof.text: Take the fibre of $\alpha$ at $\bar0'$. The sheaf convention of [def-wf-middle-extension] places $G$ in degree zero, and the shift convention $(K[1])^r=K^{r+1}$ of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] places its fibre in degree $-1$: $(G[1])_{\bar0'}=G_{\bar0'}[1]$. Hence its degree $-1$ cohomology is $G_{\bar0'}$ and its degree zero cohomology is zero. The induced fibre isomorphism is equivariant because a morphism of Weil complexes commutes with the Weil isomorphisms by [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Compare this with Step 1: the composite $H_c^1\xrightarrow{\mathcal H^{-1}(a)^{-1}}\mathcal H^{-1}(T_{\bar0'})\xrightarrow{\mathcal H^{-1}(\alpha_{\bar0'})}G_{\bar0'}$ is the asserted equivariant isomorphism, and $H_c^2\cong\mathcal H^0(T_{\bar0'})\cong0$. These are cohomology of a single shifted sheaf and composition of the two displayed isomorphisms.

source.place: paragraph 3: comparison with the single shifted sheaf, identification of H_c^1 and vanishing of H_c^2

proof.text: If $0'\notin U'_0$, apply [lem-wf-boundary-stalk-invariants] to the smooth dual line, its dense open $U'_0$, the lisse Weil sheaf $\mathcal M'$ and the closed boundary point $0'$. Its conclusion is exactly $G_{\bar0'}\simeq(\mathcal M'_{\bar\eta})^{I_{0'}}$, equivariant for the geometric Frobenius of $\kappa(0')=k_0$. The local generic stalk and its inertia action have the meaning of [d-real-boundary]; different Frobenius lifts give the same action on invariants. Compose this identification with Step 4.

source.place: paragraph 3: boundary-origin case and the Frobenius lift on inertia invariants

proof.text: If $0'\in U'_0$, restriction of the ordinary direct image gives $G_{\bar0'}=\mathcal M'_{\bar0'}$. Here $I_{0'}$, its local generic stalk and residue Frobenius lifts are those of [d-real-boundary] for the dense open $U'_0\setminus\{0'\}$ and $\mathcal M'|_{U'_0\setminus\{0'\}}$; $0'$ is a boundary point of that open. Lissity in [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves] makes each finite-level sheaf constant on a pointed etale neighbourhood of $0'$. On the strict local trait at $0'$ these trivializations identify the special and generic fibres; the inertia action on the generic fibre is trivial, since its locally constant covering already extends over that trait. Pass to the compatible integral fibres, invert $\ell$, and extend scalars as in that definition. Thus the same specialization identification is $\mathcal M'_{\bar0'}\simeq(\mathcal M'_{\bar\eta})^{I_{0'}}$. It commutes with residue Frobenius because specialization commutes with the descent map of the Weil sheaf [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]; changing a Frobenius lift multiplies by an inertia element, which acts trivially. Composing with Step 4 completes all the identifications also when the origin lies in the lisse locus.

source.place: paragraph 3: origin inside the lisse open

proof.text:
The shape: Fourier-nonexceptionality says in particular that
$\mathcal M$ is not geometrically constant, so, being unramified at
infinity, $\mathcal M$ is constituent-nonexceptional by
[lem-a1-unramified-nonexceptional], and
[prop-a1-fourier-middle-extension] gives an isomorphism of Weil
complexes
$\operatorname{FT}_\psi(j_{!*}\mathcal M[1])\cong j'_{!*}\mathcal M'[1]=j'_*\mathcal M'[1]$
with $\mathcal M'$ nonzero, irreducible and lisse.

The first identification is [lem-fd-stalk-at-origin]: the fiber of
the transform at the origin is $R\Gamma_c(\mathbf A^1,j_*\mathcal M[1])[1]$,
whose degree $-1$ part is $H_c^1(\mathbf A^1_{k_0},j_*\mathcal M)$,
while its degree $0$ part is
$H_c^2(\mathbf A^1_{k_0},j_*\mathcal M)$. This identification is
Frobenius-equivariant. Indeed, the Weil structure of
$\operatorname{FT}_\psi(K_0)$ is the one transported from those of
$K_0$ and of the kernel of [def-fd-transform] through $p_1^*$,
$\otimes$ and $p_{2,!}$, and the isomorphism of
[lem-fd-stalk-at-origin] at the rational point $0'$ is composed of
the base change isomorphism for $p_{2,!}$ along
$0'\hookrightarrow V^\vee$ and the trivialisation of the kernel on
the fibre $\mathbf A^1\times\{0'\}$ (the kernel of the zero function
$x\cdot0$ is the constant Weil sheaf). Both are natural isomorphisms
defined over $k_0$, so they commute with the Weil descent data, and the
stalk Frobenius $F_{0'}$ of the transform corresponds to the geometric
Frobenius on $R\Gamma_c(\mathbf A^1_{k_0},j_*\mathcal M)$.

For the second identification, the transformed object has the shape
$j'_*\mathcal M'[1]$ of [def-wf-middle-extension], a single
sheaf placed in degree $-1$; its fiber at the point $0'$ of the dual
line is therefore concentrated in degree $-1$, where it is the stalk
$(j'_*\mathcal M')_{0'}$, and the isomorphism of Weil complexes above
induces a Frobenius-equivariant isomorphism of the fibres at the
rational point $0'$. Comparing the two descriptions of the same fiber
gives $H_c^1(\mathbf A^1_{k_0},j_*\mathcal M)\cong(j'_*\mathcal M')_{0'}$
equivariantly, and $H_c^2(\mathbf A^1_{k_0},j_*\mathcal M)=0$
because the degree $0$ part vanishes. If $0'\notin U'_0$, the
boundary-stalk description of
[lem-wf-boundary-stalk-invariants] gives
$(j'_*\mathcal M')_{0'}=\bigl(\mathcal M'_{\bar\eta}\bigr)^{I_{0'}}$,
Frobenius-equivariantly; if $0'\in U'_0$, the inertia $I_{0'}$ acts
trivially on the lisse sheaf $\mathcal M'$ and the stalk is
$\mathcal M'_{\bar\eta}=(\mathcal M'_{\bar\eta})^{I_{0'}}$. All
cohomology is in the compact-support convention of
[def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology].
